name: Frontegg
abstract: B2B/B2C CIAM platform from Israel built for SaaS companies that need enterprise authentication without building it themselves. Flagship products include a fully hosted and embeddable Login Box (SSO via SAML/OIDC, social login, passkeys, MFA), self-service SSO/SCIM configuration for enterprise customers, an Entitlements engine that unifies RBAC, ABAC/ReBAC, feature flags and subscription plans into a single authorization API, Account Hierarchies for complex B2B org structures, a Security Center with built-in bot/brute-force/breached-password defenses and Adaptive MFA, and Frontegg.ai/AgentLink for securing AI agent and MCP-based access. Free up to 7,500 MAUs. SaaS-only deployment with EU/US data residency options.

plans.name: Pay as You Go
plans.price: Free up to 7,500 MAUs; includes hosted login, 5 enterprise (SSO/SCIM) connections, unlimited organizations, custom domain; usage-based beyond free tier

plans.name: Enterprise
plans.price: Custom (add-ons, multiple environments, advanced fraud protection, 99.99% uptime SLA, premium support)

featureList.description: Email-and-password authentication with configurable strength policy (predefined Easy/Medium levels or custom rules for length, casing, digits, special characters), password history, and expiration settings.
OAuth social login toggled per application in the Login Box builder, covering providers such as Google, Microsoft, GitHub, Facebook, Slack and others.
FIDO2/WebAuthn passkeys supported as a primary authentication method alongside password and social login.
Magic links and email-based magic codes (OTP) for passwordless sign-in. Default link/code expiration is 5 minutes, configurable between 1 minute and 1 hour; single-use tokens.
SMS-based one-time code sign-in as an alternative passwordless credential.
Clickable one-time login links delivered by email; user enters their email, receives a link, and is logged in on click. Customizable email templates.
Frontegg's identity model requires a real authenticated user (typically identified by email). No documented anonymous/guest session primitive exists.
Authenticator app (TOTP) MFA compatible with Google Authenticator, Authy, LastPass Authenticator, Microsoft Authenticator and similar apps.
Frontegg's documented authenticator-app MFA is TOTP-based only; counter-based HOTP is not offered as a distinct factor.
Security Keys (WebAuthn cross-platform authenticators such as YubiKeys) are one of Frontegg's four native MFA methods, covering roaming/U2F-class hardware keys.
WebAuthn is supported both as Security Keys (roaming authenticators) and Built-in Authenticators (platform biometrics such as Touch ID / Windows Hello).

Email OTP is offered as a first-factor passwordless login method, but Frontegg's documented MFA methods (Authenticator Apps, SMS, Security Keys, Built-in Authenticators) do not include email code as a second factor.
SMS is one of Frontegg's four native MFA methods: users receive a code by SMS and enter it to complete authentication.
Frontegg does not ship its own push-notification authenticator app. Push-based approval (e.g. Duo Push) is only available indirectly by federating to Cisco Duo as a SAML SSO identity provider.
Adaptive MFA analyzes contextual risk signals (device type, location, IP, login behavior) in real time and prompts for additional verification when risk exceeds a threshold.

Cisco Duo integrates with Frontegg via Duo's SAML SSO identity provider, letting Duo handle push/WebAuthn/security-key challenges before returning an assertion to Frontegg; this is a federation pattern rather than a native Duo API integration.
Step-up authentication can be required before sensitive actions (bulk deletes, permission changes, large transactions, data exports), prompting OTP or WebAuthn re-verification.
Frontegg implements OpenID Connect by default as part of its hosted login/identity provider offering, including a discovery document and JWKS-based token validation.
SAML 2.0 is supported both for consuming enterprise customer SSO (Service Provider) and via Frontegg's own SAML/OIDC identity provider endpoints for downstream integrations.
No WS-Federation support is documented; enterprise federation is built on SAML 2.0 and OIDC only.
Client Credentials-based M2M tokens for user-context and tenant-context service-to-service authentication, managed via Client ID/API key pairs.
Per-tenant OIDC SSO connections configurable via Management Portal or self-service, with JIT provisioning.
Per-tenant SAML 2.0 SSO connections supporting Okta, Azure AD/Entra ID, Google Workspace and others, with JIT provisioning and SAML attribute/role mapping built in.
No direct on-premises LDAP/Active Directory connector is documented; AD environments are integrated via SAML/OIDC federation (e.g., ADFS, Entra ID) or SCIM.
Microsoft Entra ID (Azure AD) is a documented SSO identity provider (SAML) and SCIM provisioning source.
Bulk user migration via API (up to 1,000 users per batch) or CSV upload.

Bulk migration supports importing existing password hashes in Bcrypt, Scrypt, Firebase (Firebase Scrypt), Argon2 and PBKDF2 formats; unsupported hash types fall back to a forced password reset on next login.
Users can be retrieved via the paginated user search/list API with exact and fuzzy filtering; no dedicated one-click bulk export/download feature is documented.
Individual user update, lock and disable operations are available via the Management API; no dedicated batch update/delete endpoint is documented.
Frontegg's primary identifier is email; imported users can bring phone numbers as well, but non-email username identifiers are not a first-class concept.
SCIM 2.0 inbound provisioning from enterprise IdPs (Okta, Microsoft Entra ID, etc.) syncing users into Frontegg tenants, configurable via Management Portal or self-service.
Frontegg acts as a SCIM consumer (inbound) rather than exposing itself as a SCIM server to downstream applications.
SCIM group sync from upstream IdPs is part of the standard SCIM 2.0 provisioning implementation.
Just-in-time user provisioning on first SSO login is included out of the box with SAML/OIDC SSO connections.
An embeddable self-service Admin Portal lets end users and tenant admins manage profile, security, SSO, SCIM and members without developer effort.
Users are automatically merged when they authenticate with different login methods (e.g., password and social login) using the same email address.
Users can be locked (login prevented without data loss) or disabled per account/tenant via the Management API.
A general-purpose metadata property is available for storing custom user data.
Secure user metadata (vendorMetadata) stores sensitive, internal/admin-only data on the user object, analogous to app metadata.
Exact and fuzzy search across user fields (name, email, metadata, ID) via the Management API.
Role-based access control with custom roles and permissions, assignable globally or per tenant, integrated into the broader Entitlements engine.
Accounts (tenants) are Frontegg's core multi-tenancy primitive, extended by Account Hierarchies that let a parent account nest sub-accounts with cascading roles.
Predefined strength levels (Easy/Medium) or custom rules for length, casing, digits and special characters, configurable at environment or account level, plus password history and expiration.
The Entitlements engine unifies RBAC, ReBAC and ABAC, evaluating user, resource and environment attributes for context-aware access decisions.
Entitlements provide fine-grained, feature-level access control down to individual features, plans and feature flags, with a visual dashboard for building product bundles.
M2M and user API tokens carry scoped roles/permissions; tenant-level Client Credentials tokens support account-wide API authorization.
ISO 27001:2022 certified, along with related ISO 27701 (privacy), 27017 (cloud security) and 27018 (PII in the cloud) certifications.

Frontegg positions itself as suitable for HIPAA-compliant deployments in its marketing content, but the official Trust Center page lists only SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 as formal certifications; BAA availability is not explicitly documented.
Frontegg does not process payment card data and PCI DSS is not listed among its Trust Center certifications.
No FedRAMP authorization is listed on Frontegg's official Trust Center; Frontegg is a commercial SaaS platform not targeting US federal workloads.
GDPR data portability is addressed via the Trust Center privacy commitments and per-user data retrieval through the Management API.
Users and their data can be permanently deleted via the Management API in line with GDPR right-to-erasure obligations described in Frontegg's privacy policy.
No dedicated consent management (marketing opt-in, granular data-processing consent) feature is documented beyond standard OAuth scope consent.
Frontegg stores/processes personal data in the EU by default, with the option to choose US-based storage instead.
Frontegg is a SaaS-only, multi-tenant platform with no documented self-hosted or single-tenant private cloud offering.
Audit events are recorded and exposed via the Audits API and end-user self-service audit section (with a download option).
Security Center is a dedicated product area providing MFA management, brute-force/bot/suspicious-IP/breached-password defenses, device fingerprinting and analytics of security events.
Customer data is encrypted at rest using modern encryption algorithms per Frontegg's Trust Center security page.
All data in transit is encrypted per Frontegg's Trust Center security page.
No BYOK / customer-managed encryption key offering is documented.
Bot detection uses proprietary algorithms by default, with optional Google reCAPTCHA for adjustable strictness.
Built-in brute-force protection with visibility into attempts via Analytics → Security Events.
Suspicious IP Detection and Impossible Travel Protection are among Frontegg's built-in security defenses.
Breached Password Protection is one of Frontegg's built-in security defenses, screening credentials against known breach data.
No continuous dark-web credential monitoring product is documented beyond point-in-time breached password screening.
Device fingerprinting and new-device detection are built-in security rules feeding into the Security Center risk signals.

Login Box and Admin Portal branding (logo, colors, layout, localizations) are configurable via theme options at the environment/application level; explicit per-individual-tenant branding overrides are not documented.
Security and MFA policies can be configured at the environment level or overridden per account (tenant) for stricter enforcement.
A fully hosted, customizable Login Box supports all authentication methods including social, SSO and passkeys.
The Login Box and Admin Portal can be embedded directly into applications via framework SDKs (React, Angular, Vue, vanilla JS) rather than only redirect-based hosting.
Login Box and Admin Portal appearance can be fully re-themed, but explicit removal of any Frontegg-branding element is not documented as a distinct feature/plan entitlement.
Built-in support for 25 languages across the login box and self-service portal, with per-language overrides via a localizations configuration object.
Prebuilt Login Box and Admin Portal UI components ship via official React, Angular, Vue and vanilla JS SDKs.
Analytics dashboards including Security Events (brute force, suspicious IP, MFA activity) in the Frontegg portal.
Official SDKs for React, Angular, Vue and vanilla JavaScript on the frontend, plus backend/management SDKs and REST API access.
Comprehensive REST Management API covering users, accounts/tenants, SSO, SCIM, RBAC, entitlements, M2M tokens and audits.
Native and fully custom webhooks let applications subscribe to authentication and lifecycle events, with per-webhook delivery logs.
Frontegg has no hosted extensibility runtime that executes developer-supplied code; webhooks are delivered to externally hosted, developer-owned endpoints in any language.
Custom domain configuration is included even on the free tier and is set at the environment level.
No dedicated Frontegg CLI is documented; infrastructure-as-code workflows are handled through the official Terraform provider instead.
Official Terraform provider (frontegg/frontegg) manages environments, workspaces and other Frontegg resources as code, with import support for existing resources.
Frontegg does not offer Auth0-style custom database action scripts; user migration is handled via bulk API/CSV import rather than per-login delegation to a legacy store.
Native webhook events for authentication and lifecycle changes, plus a custom webhook builder for adapting payloads to third-party integrations.
Login Box supports full visual customization (colors, logo, layout, enabled methods) via the portal builder or themeOptions in SDKs.
Customizable email templates for magic links/magic codes and other transactional authentication emails via the Emails tab.
The Entitlements engine offers a visual, no-code dashboard for designing product bundles/feature access, but there is no general no-code builder for authentication flows themselves.
No document-based identity verification or biometric liveness checking is documented.
No support for W3C Verifiable Credentials or DIDs is documented.

Entitlements ties feature access to subscription Plans and supports free-trial provisioning, but this is subscription-tier gating logic rather than a full payment/billing system integration (e.g., Stripe sync).

Frontegg.ai and AgentLink provide an identity/authorization layer purpose-built for AI agents: a hosted MCP server exposing chosen API tools (Agent Connector), plus Agent IAM enforcing step-up authentication, human-in-the-loop approvals, sensitive-data masking and RBAC for agent access.

No vendor statement on PQC TLS support found. Frontegg's public API (api.frontegg.com) responds with 'server: CloudFront', indicating Frontegg is fronted by AWS CloudFront. AWS CloudFront enabled hybrid PQC key exchange (ML-KEM) by default on all existing TLS security policies in September 2025, but this is infra-inherited, not a documented Frontegg-specific claim.
No public evidence Frontegg supports ML-DSA, SLH-DSA, or FN-DSA for JWT/SAML/OIDC signing.

No public PQC roadmap, blog post, or trust-center statement was found for Frontegg. Their trust center covers SOC 2 Type II, ISO 27001, and OWASP Top 10 practices but does not mention quantum readiness.
No public evidence found that the provider supports ML-KEM or HPKE (RFC 9180) for encrypting JWE tokens, SAML assertions, or user secrets.
No public evidence found of post-quantum or hybrid X.509 digital certificate support for mTLS client authentication or federation endpoints.
No public evidence found of NIST SP 800-208 stateful hash-based signature scheme support (LMS/HSS, XMSS).
